Based on historical records and architectural studies, the oldest surviving wooden buildings in China are located at the **Nanchan Temple** (specifically its Great Buddha Hall) on Mount Wutai in Shanxi Province. These structures were completed in **782 AD**, during the reign of Emperor Dezong.

This period corresponds to the **Tang Dynasty** (618–907 AD). While there are older stone structures and ruins, the Nanchan Temple hall is widely recognized as the oldest extant wooden building in China, making it a prime example of Tang Dynasty architecture. The nearby Foguang Temple, also on Mount Wutai and dating to 857 AD, is another famous example from the same dynasty.

Exact Answer: Tang Dynasty
